ramayana-4-9-23.translation: Though I could have restrained that wicked one, Raghava, my mind would not do it, held back by respect for my brother.
ramayana-4-9-23.meaning: Sugriva would not fight his brother.
ramayana-4-9-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 9: Sugriva explains how the feud began, when Vali chased the demon Mayavi into a cave.

ramayana-4-9-24.translation: Honouring that great one, I greeted him properly, but he did not bless me with a pleased heart.
ramayana-4-9-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 9: Sugriva explains how the feud began, when Vali chased the demon Mayavi into a cave.

ramayana-4-10-1.translation: Then, wanting to please him, I tried to calm my brother, who came to me furious and agitated.
ramayana-4-10-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-2.translation: By good fortune you have come back safe and killed the enemy. You alone are my protector, I who was helpless, you the joy of the helpless.
ramayana-4-10-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-3.translation: Accept this umbrella with many ribs, like the rising full moon, with its yak-tail fan, which I hold out to you.
ramayana-4-10-3.meaning: He offers the royal symbols back.
ramayana-4-10-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-4.translation: You alone are king, worthy of honour, and I am as before. I return this kingdom to you as a trust.
ramayana-4-10-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-5.translation: Do not be angry with me, gentle one, destroyer of enemies. I beg you with my head bowed, king, with folded hands.
ramayana-4-10-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-6.translation: I was forced into kingship by the ministers and townspeople who gathered, so the empty throne would not invite conquest.
ramayana-4-10-6.meaning: He was made king by necessity.
ramayana-4-10-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-7.translation: But as I spoke so warmly, that monkey scolded me, saying Shame on you! and said many such things.
ramayana-4-10-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-8.translation: Gathering the subjects and the respected ministers, he spoke to me most insultingly in the midst of friends.
ramayana-4-10-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-9.translation: You know how that great asura Mayavi, cruel and wicked, challenged me at night, longing for battle.
ramayana-4-10-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-10.translation: Hearing his roar, I left the palace, and this cruel brother of mine quickly followed me.
ramayana-4-10-10.meaning: Vali tells his side of the story.
ramayana-4-10-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-11.translation: As soon as the mighty one saw me at night with a companion, he fled in terror. Seeing us, he ran, and chased hard, he entered a great cave.
ramayana-4-10-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-12.translation: Knowing he had entered that dreadful great cave, I said to this cruel-looking brother of mine:
ramayana-4-10-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-13.translation: I cannot go back to the city without killing him. Wait at the mouth of the cave until I kill him.
ramayana-4-10-13.meaning: Vali vowed to finish the fight.
ramayana-4-10-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-14.translation: Thinking he was standing guard, I went into that hard place. A year passed as I searched for him.
ramayana-4-10-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-15.translation: I found that fearsome enemy through persistence and killed that asura there along with his kin.
ramayana-4-10-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-16.translation: The cave was filled with the stream of blood pouring from his mouth as he roared on the ground, and it became hard to pass.
ramayana-4-10-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-17.translation: After killing that bold enemy, Dundubhi's son, as I came out I saw the mouth of the cave was closed.
ramayana-4-10-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-18.translation: I called out Sugriva! again and again, and when there was no reply I was deeply hurt.
ramayana-4-10-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-19.translation: I broke it open with many kicks, and so I got out and came back.
ramayana-4-10-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-20.translation: There I was shut in by this cruel Sugriva, who wanted the kingdom for himself and forgot a brother's love.
ramayana-4-10-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-21.translation: Having said this, the monkey Vali, without fear, drove me out with only a single garment.
ramayana-4-10-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-22.translation: Cast out by him and with my wife taken, Raghava, I wandered the whole earth with its forests and seas out of fear of him.
ramayana-4-10-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-23.translation: Grieving over the loss of my wife, I entered Rishyamuka, best of mountains, which Vali cannot approach for a certain reason.
ramayana-4-10-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-24.translation: I have told you the whole long story of the feud. See the disaster I, though innocent, have met, Raghava.
ramayana-4-10-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-25.translation: Hero who frees all the world from fear, please show me kindness by subduing Vali, for I am stricken with fear of him.
ramayana-4-10-25.meaning: He asks Rama to stop Vali.
ramayana-4-10-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-26.translation: Spoken to this way, the radiant knower of dharma began to speak words full of dharma to Sugriva, as if smiling.
ramayana-4-10-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-27.translation: These sharp, unfailing arrows of mine, bright as the sun, will fall in fury on that wrongdoer Vali.
ramayana-4-10-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-28.translation: Only until I see him, the one who took your wife, will that wicked Vali, corrupter of good conduct, stay alive.
ramayana-4-10-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-10-29.translation: Judging by my own pain, I see you sunk in an ocean of grief. I will bring you across, and you will gain all you desire.
ramayana-4-10-29.meaning: Rama understands Sugriva's pain from his own.
ramayana-4-10-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 10: Vali returns, finds Sugriva crowned, and drives him out in anger.

ramayana-4-11-1.translation: Hearing Rama's words, which increased his joy and courage, Sugriva honoured and praised Raghava.
ramayana-4-11-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-2.translation: No doubt you, in anger, could burn the worlds with your blazing sharp arrows that pierce the vitals, like the sun at the end of an age.
ramayana-4-11-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-3.translation: Hear with full attention about Vali's strength, his might and his endurance, then decide what to do next.
ramayana-4-11-3.meaning: Sugriva wants Rama to know what he faces.
ramayana-4-11-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-4.translation: Before sunrise, Vali strides from the western sea to the eastern and from the southern to the northern, without tiring.
ramayana-4-11-4.meaning: Vali can cross the world before dawn.
ramayana-4-11-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-5.translation: The mighty one climbs the tops of mountains, hurls even great peaks into the air and catches them.
ramayana-4-11-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-6.translation: Many strong trees of every kind in the forests have been broken by Vali to show off his strength.
ramayana-4-11-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-7.translation: There was a buffalo named Dundubhi, bright as a peak of Kailasa, who had the strength of a thousand elephants.
ramayana-4-11-7.meaning: Dundubhi was a mighty buffalo demon.
ramayana-4-11-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-8.translation: Swollen with pride in his strength and deluded by a boon, that huge wicked one went to the ocean, lord of rivers.
ramayana-4-11-8.meaning: Pride led Dundubhi to seek a fight.
ramayana-4-11-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-9.translation: Passing over the wave-filled sea, that store of jewels, he said to the great ocean: Give me battle.
ramayana-4-11-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-10.translation: Then the righteous, mighty ocean rose up and spoke to the asura, who was driven by fate, O king.
ramayana-4-11-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-11.translation: I cannot give you battle, skilled fighter. Listen, I will tell you who will give you a fight.
ramayana-4-11-11.meaning: The ocean declines and redirects him.
ramayana-4-11-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-12.translation: In a great forest is the king of mountains, the best refuge of ascetics, Shiva's father-in-law, famous by the name Himavan.
ramayana-4-11-12.meaning: He sends Dundubhi to the Himalaya.
ramayana-4-11-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-13.translation: With caves and springs, many grottoes and waterfalls, he can give you matchless pleasure in battle.
ramayana-4-11-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-14.translation: Knowing the ocean was afraid, the great asura came to the Himalayan forest like an arrow loosed from a bow.
ramayana-4-11-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-15.translation: Then Dundubhi hurled down many white rocks of that mountain, huge as great elephants, and roared.
ramayana-4-11-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-16.translation: Then Himavan, shaped like a white cloud, gentle and pleasant in form, spoke standing on his own peak.
ramayana-4-11-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-17.translation: You should not trouble me, Dundubhi, lover of dharma. I am not skilled in war, I am a refuge for ascetics.
ramayana-4-11-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-18.translation: Hearing these words of the wise king of mountains, Dundubhi spoke, his eyes red with anger.
ramayana-4-11-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-19.translation: If you cannot fight, or are unwilling out of fear of me, tell me who would give me battle today, eager as I am to fight.
ramayana-4-11-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-20.translation: Hearing this, righteous Himavan, skilled in speech, spoke in anger to that great asura words he had never said before.
ramayana-4-11-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-21.translation: There is a monkey named Vali, very wise and equal to Indra in valour, glorious, who lives in matchless Kishkindha.
ramayana-4-11-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-22.translation: That wise one, skilled in war, can give you a great single combat, as Indra did to Namuchi.
ramayana-4-11-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-23.translation: Go to him quickly if you want a fight here, for he is always unbeatable and brave in battle.
ramayana-4-11-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-24.translation: Hearing Himavan's words, Dundubhi, filled with anger, went to Vali's city of Kishkindha.
ramayana-4-11-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-25.translation: He took the form of a buffalo with sharp horns, terrifying, like a great rain cloud full of water in the sky in the rainy season.
ramayana-4-11-25.meaning: He arrives as a fearsome buffalo.
ramayana-4-11-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-26.translation: Coming to the gate of Kishkindha, mighty Dundubhi roared like a war drum, shaking the earth.
ramayana-4-11-26.meaning: He roars at the city gate.
ramayana-4-11-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-27.translation: Breaking the trees nearby, tearing the earth with his hooves, he scraped the gate proudly with his horn like an elephant.
ramayana-4-11-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-28.translation: Vali, who was in the inner apartments, heard the noise and, unable to bear it, came out with his women, like the moon with the stars.
ramayana-4-11-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-29.translation: Vali, lord of monkeys and all forest creatures, spoke to Dundubhi in measured words, each syllable clear.
ramayana-4-11-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-30.translation: Why do you roar here blocking the city gate? I know you, Dundubhi. Save your life, mighty one.
ramayana-4-11-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-31.translation: Hearing these words of the wise monkey king, Dundubhi spoke with eyes red with anger.
ramayana-4-11-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-32.translation: You should not speak in front of women, hero. Give me battle, and then I will know your strength.
ramayana-4-11-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-33.translation: Or I will hold back my anger for tonight. Take your pleasures freely till sunrise, monkey.
ramayana-4-11-33.meaning: He offers Vali one last night.
ramayana-4-11-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-34.translation: Whoever kills someone like you, drunk, careless, asleep, alone or dazed with pleasure, is counted among the worst sinners in the world.
ramayana-4-11-34.meaning: Even demons held rules about fair fighting.
ramayana-4-11-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-35.translation: Laughing gently, Vali sent away all the women, Tara and the rest, and spoke angrily to that great asura.
ramayana-4-11-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-36.translation: Do not think I am drunk, if you are unafraid in battle. Take this intoxication as the hero's drink before the fight.
ramayana-4-11-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-37.translation: Having said this, enraged, he put on the golden garland given to his father by Indra and stood ready for battle.
ramayana-4-11-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-38.translation: Grabbing mountain-like Dundubhi by the horns, Vali threw him down and roared loudly.
ramayana-4-11-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-39.translation: In that deadly fight Dundubhi was crushed. Blood flowed from his ears as he was thrown, and the huge one fell to the ground dead.
ramayana-4-11-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-40.translation: Lifting the lifeless, senseless body with his arms, mighty Vali flung it a full yojana with one heave.
ramayana-4-11-40.meaning: Vali hurls the carcass far away.
ramayana-4-11-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-41.translation: As it was flung, drops of blood from its mouth, carried by the wind, fell toward Matanga's hermitage.
ramayana-4-11-41.meaning: Blood fell on a sage's hermitage.
ramayana-4-11-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-42.translation: Seeing the drops of blood fallen there, the sage laid a great curse on Vali who had thrown it: He must not enter here; if he enters he will die.
ramayana-4-11-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-43.translation: Vali went to the great sage and begged him with folded hands.
ramayana-4-11-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-44.translation: Since then, afraid of the curse, the monkey does not wish to enter or even look at the great mountain Rishyamuka, lord of men.
ramayana-4-11-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-45.translation: Knowing he cannot enter, Rama, I wander this great forest with my ministers, free from despair.
ramayana-4-11-45.meaning: This is why Sugriva is safe here.
ramayana-4-11-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-46.translation: Here is Dundubhi's heap of bones, huge like a mountain peak, thrown down because of Vali's pride in his strength.
ramayana-4-11-46.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-47.translation: And these are seven great sal trees with hanging branches, any one of which Vali can strip of leaves by his strength.
ramayana-4-11-47.meaning: Vali can shake the leaves off huge trees.
ramayana-4-11-47.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-48.translation: I have shown you his unmatched strength, Rama. How will you be able to kill Vali in battle, king?
ramayana-4-11-48.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-49.translation: If you could split these sal trees with a single arrow, then I would know you are able to kill Vali, mighty-armed one.
ramayana-4-11-49.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-50.translation: Hearing great Sugriva's words, mighty-armed Raghava lifted Dundubhi's body playfully with his big toe and flung it ten yojanas.
ramayana-4-11-50.meaning: Rama tosses the skeleton with ease.
ramayana-4-11-50.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-51.translation: Seeing the body thrown, Sugriva again spoke meaningful words to Rama in front of Lakshmana.
ramayana-4-11-51.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-11-52.translation: Friend, the body was wet and full of fresh flesh when it was thrown before. Now it is light, fleshless, like straw, Raghava. One cannot tell from this whether your strength or his is greater.
ramayana-4-11-52.meaning: A dry skeleton is no fair test.
ramayana-4-11-52.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 11: Sugriva describes Vali's immense strength, the killing of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi, and the curse that keeps Vali off Rishyamuka.

ramayana-4-12-1.translation: Hearing Sugriva's well-spoken words, radiant Rama took up his bow to give him confidence.
ramayana-4-12-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-2.translation: Taking the fearsome bow and a single arrow, the giver of honour aimed at the sal trees and shot, filling the directions with the twang of the string.
ramayana-4-12-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-3.translation: Released by the mighty one, the gold-adorned arrow split the seven sal trees on the hillside and entered the earth.
ramayana-4-12-3.meaning: One arrow pierces all seven trees.
ramayana-4-12-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-4.translation: In a moment the swift arrow pierced the earth, came out again and quickly went back into Rama's own quiver.
ramayana-4-12-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-5.translation: Seeing the seven sal trees pierced, the chief of monkeys was utterly amazed at the speed of Rama's arrow.
ramayana-4-12-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-6.translation: Overjoyed, Sugriva fell with his head to the ground before Raghava, his ornaments hanging down, with folded hands.
ramayana-4-12-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-7.translation: Delighted by that deed, he said to Rama, knower of dharma, the best of all who know weapons, the hero standing there:
ramayana-4-12-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-8.translation: With your arrows you could kill even all the gods with Indra in battle, best of men. How much more Vali, lord!
ramayana-4-12-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-9.translation: Who could stand before you in battle, Kakutstha, when with one arrow you split seven great sal trees, a hill and the earth?
ramayana-4-12-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-10.translation: Today my grief is gone and my joy is supreme, having found you as a friend, like great Indra and Varuna.
ramayana-4-12-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-11.translation: For my sake, Kakutstha, kill Vali this very day, my enemy in the form of a brother. Here I fold my hands to you.
ramayana-4-12-11.meaning: He asks Rama to act now.
ramayana-4-12-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

keywords.meaning: in the form of a brother

ramayana-4-12-12.translation: Then wise Rama embraced the handsome Sugriva and replied with words Lakshmana approved:
ramayana-4-12-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-13.translation: Let us go from here to Kishkindha. Go quickly ahead, Sugriva, and when you get there, challenge Vali, who is a brother only in name.
ramayana-4-12-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-14.translation: They all went quickly to Vali's city of Kishkindha and stood hidden among the trees in the thick forest.
ramayana-4-12-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-15.translation: Sugriva, his garment tied tight, roared terribly to call Vali out, as if splitting the sky with his cries.
ramayana-4-12-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-16.translation: Hearing his brother's roar, mighty Vali, enraged, rushed out like the sun from the edge of the setting mountain.
ramayana-4-12-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-17.translation: Then a tumultuous fight broke out between Vali and Sugriva, terrible like that of the planets Mercury and Mars in the sky.
ramayana-4-12-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-18.translation: The two brothers, mad with rage, struck each other in battle with palms like lightning and fists like thunderbolts.
ramayana-4-12-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama pierces seven sal trees with one arrow; Sugriva challenges Vali and is beaten because Rama cannot tell the brothers apart.

ramayana-4-12-19.translation: Then Rama, bow in hand, looked at the two heroes, who were as alike as the twin Ashvin gods.
ramayana-4-12-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-20.translation: Because Raghava could not tell Sugriva from Vali, he did not decide to release his deadly arrow.
ramayana-4-12-20.meaning: Rama holds his fire to avoid hitting his friend.
ramayana-4-12-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-21.translation: Meanwhile Sugriva, beaten by Vali and not seeing Raghava his protector, fled to Rishyamuka.
ramayana-4-12-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-22.translation: Exhausted, his body soaked in blood and battered by blows, chased by the angry Vali, he entered the great forest.
ramayana-4-12-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-23.translation: Seeing him enter the forest, mighty Vali, afraid of the curse, said You are spared and turned back.
ramayana-4-12-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-24.translation: Raghava too, with his brother and Hanuman, came to the same forest where Sugriva was.
ramayana-4-12-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-25.translation: Seeing Rama come with Lakshmana, Sugriva, ashamed, spoke miserably, looking at the ground.
ramayana-4-12-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-26.translation: You told me to challenge him, showed me your power, then let my enemy beat me. What have you done now?
ramayana-4-12-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-27.translation: You should have told me truly at that moment, Raghava, I will not kill Vali. Then I would not have gone from here.
ramayana-4-12-27.meaning: He wishes Rama had been honest.
ramayana-4-12-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-28.translation: As great Sugriva spoke so piteously in a miserable voice, Raghava spoke again.
ramayana-4-12-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-29.translation: Sugriva, my friend, listen and let go of your anger. Here is why I did not release this arrow.
ramayana-4-12-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-30.translation: In ornaments, dress, size and gait, you and Vali are alike, Sugriva.
ramayana-4-12-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-31.translation: In voice, radiance, glance, valour and speech, monkey, I could not tell you two apart.
ramayana-4-12-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-32.translation: So, confused by your likeness, best of monkeys, I did not loose my swift, enemy-destroying arrow.
ramayana-4-12-32.meaning: He feared hitting the wrong brother.
ramayana-4-12-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-33.translation: But within a moment you will see Vali struck down in battle by one arrow from me, writhing on the ground.
ramayana-4-12-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-34.translation: Make a mark of recognition on yourself, lord of monkeys, so I can know you when you are fighting him.
ramayana-4-12-34.meaning: They need a way to tell him apart.
ramayana-4-12-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-35.translation: Lakshmana, pull up this flowering gajapushpi vine with its lovely marks and put it around great Sugriva's neck.
ramayana-4-12-35.meaning: Rama asks Lakshmana to garland Sugriva.
ramayana-4-12-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-36.translation: Then Lakshmana pulled up the flowering gajapushpi growing on the hillside and placed it around his neck.
ramayana-4-12-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-37.translation: With the vine around his neck, glorious Sugriva shone like a rain cloud at twilight with a garland of cranes.
ramayana-4-12-37.meaning: The garland makes Sugriva stand out.
ramayana-4-12-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-12-38.translation: Shining in body and reassured by Rama's words, he went with Rama to Kishkindha, which Vali ruled.
ramayana-4-12-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 12: Rama cannot tell the brothers apart in the fight, so Sugriva is beaten; Lakshmana marks him with a flowering vine.

ramayana-4-13-1.translation: Righteous Rama, Lakshmana's elder brother, went with Sugriva from Rishyamuka to Kishkindha, guarded by Vali's might.
ramayana-4-13-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-2.translation: Rama raised his great gold-adorned bow and took arrows bright as the sun, made for victory.
ramayana-4-13-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-3.translation: Ahead of great Raghava went sturdy-necked Sugriva and mighty Lakshmana.
ramayana-4-13-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-4.translation: Behind came heroic Hanuman, Nala, the monkey Nila and radiant Tara, leaders of monkey troops.
ramayana-4-13-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-5.translation: They looked at the trees weighed down with flowers and the clear rivers flowing to the sea,
ramayana-4-13-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-6.translation: the grottoes, hills, waterfalls and caves, the chief peaks and lovely valleys,
ramayana-4-13-6.meaning: The land is varied and beautiful.
ramayana-4-13-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-7.translation: and along the way they saw ponds full of water, adorned with leaves clear as beryl and lotuses with opening buds.
ramayana-4-13-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-8.translation: They rang with karandava ducks, cranes, swans, vanjula birds, water fowl, chakravakas and other birds.
ramayana-4-13-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-9.translation: They saw deer roaming everywhere on the open ground, fearless forest dwellers feeding on tender grass shoots.
ramayana-4-13-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-10.translation: And wild elephants, fierce, roaming alone, with white tusks, enemies of the ponds, breaking down the banks.
ramayana-4-13-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-11.translation: Seeing other forest creatures and birds flying through the sky, Sugriva's followers went on quickly.
ramayana-4-13-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-12.translation: As they hurried on, Rama, joy of the Raghus, saw a forest thick with trees and said to Sugriva:
ramayana-4-13-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-13.translation: This cluster of trees shines like a cloud in the sky, vast as a mass of clouds and ringed with banana plants.
ramayana-4-13-13.meaning: The grove looks like a cloud.
ramayana-4-13-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-14.translation: What is this? I wish to know, friend, I am curious. I would like you to satisfy my curiosity.
ramayana-4-13-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-15.translation: Hearing great Raghava's words, Sugriva told him about that great forest as they walked.
ramayana-4-13-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-16.translation: This, Raghava, is a vast hermitage that removes weariness, rich in gardens and groves, with sweet roots, fruits and water.
ramayana-4-13-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-17.translation: Here lived seven sages called the Saptajanas, firm in their vows, who always lay in water with their heads down.
ramayana-4-13-17.meaning: Seven sages practised severe austerity here.
ramayana-4-13-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-18.translation: Living in the forest and eating only air every seventh night, after seven hundred years they went to heaven in their bodies.
ramayana-4-13-18.meaning: Their austerity took them to heaven.
ramayana-4-13-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-19.translation: By their power this hermitage, walled by trees, cannot be entered even by the gods and demons with Indra.
ramayana-4-13-19.meaning: Their power still guards the place.
ramayana-4-13-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-20.translation: Birds and other forest creatures avoid it. Those who enter it by mistake never come back.
ramayana-4-13-20.meaning: The place is sacred and dangerous.
ramayana-4-13-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-21.translation: Here one hears the sound of ornaments with clear syllables, the sounds of instruments and singing, and a divine fragrance, Raghava.
ramayana-4-13-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-22.translation: The three sacred fires still burn, and this smoke can be seen, thick and dusky red like a dove's body, wrapping the treetops.
ramayana-4-13-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-23.translation: Righteous Raghava, bow to them with your brother Lakshmana, pure and with folded hands.
ramayana-4-13-23.meaning: Sugriva asks Rama to show respect.
ramayana-4-13-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-24.translation: No harm is seen in the body of those who bow to those sages of perfected soul, Rama.
ramayana-4-13-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-25.translation: Then Rama with his brother Lakshmana, hands folded, paid respect to those great sages.
ramayana-4-13-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-26.translation: Having paid respect, righteous Rama, his brother Lakshmana, Sugriva and the monkeys went on with glad hearts.
ramayana-4-13-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-13-27.translation: Going a long way from that hermitage of the Saptajanas, they saw Kishkindha, hard to attack, guarded by Vali.
ramayana-4-13-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 13: on the way back to Kishkindha, the party passes and honours the hermitage of the Saptajana sages.

ramayana-4-14-1.translation: They all went quickly to Kishkindha, guarded by Vali, and stood hidden behind trees in the thick forest.
ramayana-4-14-1.meaning: They take cover near the city.
ramayana-4-14-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-2.translation: Looking all around the forest, Sugriva, fond of forests and broad-necked, worked himself into a fierce anger.
ramayana-4-14-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-3.translation: Then, surrounded by his companions, he roared terribly and challenged Vali to battle, as if splitting the sky with his cries.
ramayana-4-14-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-4.translation: Then Sugriva, bright as the young sun and moving like a proud lion, seeing Rama skilled in action, spoke:
ramayana-4-14-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-5.translation: We have reached Vali's city of Kishkindha, full of monkeys as if netted, with gateways of refined gold and rich in flags and machines.
ramayana-4-14-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-6.translation: Hero, make your earlier promise to kill Vali come true quickly, as the season brings a vine to fruit.
ramayana-4-14-6.meaning: Sugriva asks Rama to keep his word.
ramayana-4-14-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-7.translation: Spoken to this way by Sugriva, righteous Raghava, destroyer of enemies, replied:
ramayana-4-14-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-8.translation: You bear a mark of recognition with this gajapushpi, like the sun in the sky ringed with a garland of stars.
ramayana-4-14-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-9.translation: Today, monkey, with a single arrow in battle I will free you from the fear and enmity Vali has caused.
ramayana-4-14-9.meaning: Rama vows to end Sugriva's fear.
ramayana-4-14-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-10.translation: Show me your enemy, Sugriva, who has the form of a brother, and Vali will be killed and rolling in the dust of the forest.
ramayana-4-14-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-11.translation: If he comes into my sight and goes back alive, then let me be blamed, and you may condemn me at once.
ramayana-4-14-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-12.translation: You saw me split the seven sal trees with an arrow. So know that by my strength Vali is as good as dead today.
ramayana-4-14-12.meaning: Rama reminds him of the proof.
ramayana-4-14-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-13.translation: I have never spoken a falsehood, hero, even in hardship, and bound by love of dharma I never will.
ramayana-4-14-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-14.translation: I will make my promise fruitful. Drop your worry, as Indra makes the rice in the field ripen with rain.
ramayana-4-14-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-15.translation: So, Sugriva, make that sound to call out gold-garlanded Vali, by which the monkey will rush out.
ramayana-4-14-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-16.translation: Proud of his victories, boasting of conquest, not beaten by you before, Vali who loves a fight will rush out from the city without hesitation.
ramayana-4-14-16.meaning: Vali's pride will draw him out.
ramayana-4-14-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-17.translation: Heroes who know their own strength do not tolerate insult from enemies in battle, especially in front of women.
ramayana-4-14-17.meaning: Pride will not let Vali refuse.
ramayana-4-14-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-18.translation: Hearing Rama's words, golden-tawny Sugriva roared a cruel roar, as if tearing the sky apart.
ramayana-4-14-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-19.translation: Frightened by the sound, cows ran off, their lustre gone, like noblewomen thrown into turmoil when a king's misrule touches them.
ramayana-4-14-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-20.translation: Deer ran swiftly like horses routed in battle, and birds fell to the ground like planets whose merit is spent.
ramayana-4-14-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-14-21.translation: Then the son of the Sun, confident, his fire swelling with courage, quickly let out a roar like a mass of thunderclouds, like the ocean with its waves tossed by the wind.
ramayana-4-14-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 14: Sugriva roars a second challenge at Kishkindha, reassured by Rama's promise.

ramayana-4-15-1.translation: Vali, in the inner apartments, heard that roar of his great brother Sugriva and could not bear it.
ramayana-4-15-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-2.translation: Hearing his roar that shook all beings, his intoxication vanished at once and a great anger fell on him.
ramayana-4-15-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-3.translation: Vali, his body seized by rage, glowing like the twilight sun, suddenly lost his lustre like the eclipsed sun.
ramayana-4-15-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-4.translation: Vali, fierce with his fangs and like a blazing fire in anger, looked like a lake with lotuses torn up along with their stalks.
ramayana-4-15-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-5.translation: Hearing that unbearable sound, the monkey rushed out, as if splitting the earth with his heavy strides.
ramayana-4-15-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-6.translation: But Tara embraced him lovingly, showing her care, and, frightened and anxious, spoke these well-meant words.
ramayana-4-15-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-7.translation: Hero, give up this anger that has come like a river's flood, as one rising from bed in the morning throws off a used garland.
ramayana-4-15-7.meaning: Tara asks Vali to let go of anger.
ramayana-4-15-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-8.translation: I do not like you rushing out so suddenly. Listen, I will tell you why you are being stopped.
ramayana-4-15-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-9.translation: He came before in anger and challenged you to battle. You came out, beat him, and he fled in all directions.
ramayana-4-15-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-10.translation: For him, beaten and especially hurt by you, to come back and challenge you again makes me suspicious.
ramayana-4-15-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-11.translation: The pride and resolve in his roar and its fury are no small matter.
ramayana-4-15-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-12.translation: I do not think Sugriva has come here without help. He has some support behind him that he relies on as he roars.
ramayana-4-15-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-13.translation: The monkey is clever and wise by nature. Sugriva will not go with someone whose strength he has not tested.
ramayana-4-15-13.meaning: Sugriva would choose a strong ally.
ramayana-4-15-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-14.translation: Hero, I heard earlier what young prince Angada said. I will tell you these words for your good.
ramayana-4-15-14.meaning: Tara shares news from their son.
ramayana-4-15-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-15.translation: Your brother's famous ally, harsh in battle, is Rama, crusher of enemy armies, like the fire rising at the end of an age.
ramayana-4-15-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

keywords.meaning: fire at the end of an age

ramayana-4-15-16.translation: He is a sheltering tree for good people, the highest refuge of those in trouble, the shelter of the suffering, and the one vessel of fame.
ramayana-4-15-16.meaning: Rama protects the good and the suffering.
ramayana-4-15-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-17.translation: Full of knowledge and wisdom, devoted to his father's command, he is a great mine of virtues, as the king of mountains is of minerals.
ramayana-4-15-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-18.translation: So it is not wise for you to oppose that great soul Rama, unconquerable and immeasurable in battle.
ramayana-4-15-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-19.translation: Hero, I will tell you something, and I do not wish to find fault. Listen and do what I say for your good.
ramayana-4-15-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-20.translation: Quickly and rightly crown Sugriva as crown prince. Do not quarrel, hero king, with your stronger brother.
ramayana-4-15-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-21.translation: I think it right for you to make friends with Rama and be loving to Sugriva, casting enmity far away.
ramayana-4-15-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-22.translation: This younger brother, the monkey, deserves your care. Whether there or here, he is in every way your kin.
ramayana-4-15-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-15-23.translation: If you would do what pleases me, and if you know I want your good, then I beg you earnestly, follow my sound advice.
ramayana-4-15-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 15: Vali's wife Tara warns him not to go out, since Sugriva must have Rama's backing.

ramayana-4-16-1.translation: As Tara, whose face was like the moon, spoke this way, Vali rebuked her and said:
ramayana-4-16-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-2.translation: Why should I tolerate the fury of this roaring brother, who is especially my enemy, lovely one?
ramayana-4-16-2.meaning: Vali will not ignore the challenge.
ramayana-4-16-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-3.translation: For heroes who have never been defeated and never retreat in battle, bearing an insult is worse than death, timid one.
ramayana-4-16-3.meaning: Pride makes insult unbearable to him.
ramayana-4-16-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-4.translation: I cannot bear the fury of Sugriva, eager for a fight and roaring, though he is weaker.
ramayana-4-16-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-5.translation: And you need not worry about Raghava on my account. He knows dharma and is grateful. How would he do wrong?
ramayana-4-16-5.meaning: Vali trusts Rama to be fair.
ramayana-4-16-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-6.translation: Go back with the women. Why do you follow me further? You have shown your love, Tara, and your devotion to me.
ramayana-4-16-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-7.translation: I will go and fight Sugriva. Drop your fear. I will crush his pride, but he will not lose his life.
ramayana-4-16-7.meaning: Vali means only to humble him.
ramayana-4-16-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-8.translation: I make you swear by my life and by my victory, go back. I will return after beating that brother in battle.
ramayana-4-16-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-9.translation: Then sweet-spoken Tara embraced Vali and, weeping softly, walked around him respectfully, keeping him to her right.
ramayana-4-16-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-10.translation: Then, wishing him victory, she recited blessings with mantras and, dazed with grief, went into the inner apartments with the women.
ramayana-4-16-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-11.translation: When Tara had gone home with the women, Vali left the city in anger, hissing like a great snake.
ramayana-4-16-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-12.translation: Sighing, the swift and furious Vali cast his eyes all around, eager to see his enemy.
ramayana-4-16-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-13.translation: Then glorious Vali saw golden-tawny Sugriva, well girded and firm, blazing like fire.
ramayana-4-16-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-14.translation: Seeing mighty Sugriva standing ready, the furious Vali tightened his garment.
ramayana-4-16-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-15.translation: Girded tight, mighty Vali raised his fist and, seizing the moment, went straight at Sugriva to fight.
ramayana-4-16-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-16.translation: Sugriva too raised his clenched fist and came at gold-garlanded Vali in greater fury.
ramayana-4-16-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-17.translation: Vali, eyes red with anger, said this to Sugriva, skilled in battle, as he rushed at him with great speed:
ramayana-4-16-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-18.translation: This fist I have clenched tight, fingers set firm, released with force, will take your life as it goes.
ramayana-4-16-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-19.translation: Told this, Sugriva angrily said to Vali: Let my fist fall on your head and take your life.
ramayana-4-16-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-20.translation: Struck by him, Vali rushed at him in rage, spouting blood like a mountain with streams gushing out.
ramayana-4-16-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-21.translation: Sugriva easily uprooted a sal tree and with force struck Vali on the limbs, like a thunderbolt hitting a great mountain.
ramayana-4-16-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-22.translation: Vali, shaken by the blow of the sal tree, reeled like a boat overloaded on the sea.
ramayana-4-16-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-23.translation: The two, terrible in strength and courage, swift as Garuda, swelled in fierce forms like the moon and sun in the sky.
ramayana-4-16-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-24.translation: Sugriva, his pride broken by Vali and his strength waning, still in anger showed his quickness against Vali.
ramayana-4-16-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-25.translation: Then Raghava fitted to his bow an arrow like a venomous snake, and the great arrow struck Vali's chest.
ramayana-4-16-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-26.translation: Struck with force, Vali fell to the ground.
ramayana-4-16-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-16-27.translation: Drenched in streams of blood like a flowering ashoka shaken by the wind, the son of Indra fell senseless to the earth in battle like Indra's banner thrown down.
ramayana-4-16-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 16: Vali ignores Tara, fights Sugriva, and is struck down by Rama's arrow.

ramayana-4-17-1.translation: Struck by Rama's arrow, Vali, harsh in battle, fell suddenly like a felled tree.
ramayana-4-17-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-2.translation: With all his limbs stretched on the ground and his ornaments of refined gold, he fell like the banner of the king of gods with its ropes cut.
ramayana-4-17-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-3.translation: When the lord of monkeys and bears fell, the earth lost its brightness like the sky without the moon.
ramayana-4-17-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-4.translation: Even as the great one lay on the ground, his body was not left by glory, life, splendour or valour.
ramayana-4-17-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-5.translation: The fine golden garland set with gems, given by Indra, held the life, splendour and glory of the monkey chief.
ramayana-4-17-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-6.translation: With that golden garland the hero, leader of monkeys, looked like a rain cloud edged with twilight.
ramayana-4-17-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-7.translation: His garland, his body, and the arrow that pierced his vitals, like beauty made in three parts, shone even as he lay fallen.
ramayana-4-17-7.meaning: The scene has a strange beauty.
ramayana-4-17-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-8.translation: That weapon, shot from Rama's bow, which opens the way to heaven, brought the hero to the highest state.
ramayana-4-17-8.meaning: Death by Rama's arrow leads to heaven.
ramayana-4-17-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-9.translation: Fallen in battle like a fire whose flames are gone, like Yayati fallen from heaven when his merit was spent,
ramayana-4-17-9.meaning: Vali is likened to fallen greatness.
ramayana-4-17-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-10.translation: like the sun thrown down to earth by Time at the end of an age, unconquerable like great Indra, unbearable like great Indra,
ramayana-4-17-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-11.translation: Vali, son of great Indra, wearing a golden garland, lion-chested, mighty-armed, with a blazing face and tawny eyes, lay fallen. Rama, followed by Lakshmana, saw him and approached.
ramayana-4-17-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-12.translation: Seeing Raghava and mighty Lakshmana, Vali spoke words that were courteous yet harsh, and grounded in dharma.
ramayana-4-17-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-13.translation: What merit have you gained by killing one who was facing away? I was absorbed in fighting and met my death because of you.
ramayana-4-17-13.meaning: Vali charges Rama with an unfair blow.
ramayana-4-17-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-14.translation: Rama is well born, strong in character, radiant, keeps his vows, feels compassion and is devoted to the good of the people.
ramayana-4-17-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-15.translation: He is kind, very energetic, knows what is proper, and is firm in his vows. So all beings proclaim your fame on earth.
ramayana-4-17-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-16.translation: Weighing those virtues and your noble birth, I came to fight Sugriva even though Tara tried to stop me.
ramayana-4-17-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-17.translation: Before I saw you, I thought: He will not shoot me while I am engaged and off guard with another.
ramayana-4-17-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-18.translation: I did not know you were a destroyer of your own soul, unrighteous behind a banner of righteousness, wicked in conduct, like a well covered with grass.
ramayana-4-17-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-19.translation: Wearing the dress of the good, you are sinful, like a hidden fire. I did not recognise you, cloaked in the disguise of dharma.
ramayana-4-17-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-20.translation: I did you no harm in your land or your city, nor did I insult you. Why do you kill me, who am blameless?
ramayana-4-17-20.meaning: Vali says he did Rama no wrong.
ramayana-4-17-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-21.translation: A monkey who lives in the forest, always eating fruits and roots, who was not fighting you but someone else.
ramayana-4-17-21.meaning: Vali stresses he was no threat to Rama.
ramayana-4-17-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-22.translation: You are a king's son, trusted and handsome, and you bear the outward signs of dharma, king.
ramayana-4-17-22.meaning: Rama looks like a righteous prince.
ramayana-4-17-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-23.translation: Who, born in a warrior family, learned and free of doubt, would hide behind the signs of dharma and do a cruel deed?
ramayana-4-17-23.meaning: A true kshatriya would not act this way.
ramayana-4-17-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-24.translation: Rama, born in a royal line and famed as righteous, why do you go about unworthy in a worthy form?
ramayana-4-17-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-25.translation: Conciliation, generosity, forgiveness, dharma, truth, steadiness and valour are the virtues of kings, king, and punishment for wrongdoers.
ramayana-4-17-25.meaning: Vali lists the virtues of kings.
ramayana-4-17-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-26.translation: We are forest creatures, Rama, animals eating roots and fruits. That is our nature, while you are a man, a lord of men.
ramayana-4-17-26.meaning: Vali sets monkeys apart from human law.
ramayana-4-17-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-27.translation: Land, gold and silver are the reasons for conflict. What greed could you have for the forest or for my fruits?
ramayana-4-17-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-28.translation: Policy and discipline, punishment and favour: the conduct of kings is ordered, and kings do not act on whim.
ramayana-4-17-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-29.translation: But you are ruled by desire, angry, unsteady, careless of royal duties, and quick to use the bow.
ramayana-4-17-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-30.translation: You have no regard for dharma, your mind is not set on what is right, and you are dragged by the senses, acting on whim, lord of men.
ramayana-4-17-30.meaning: He accuses Rama of losing his way.
ramayana-4-17-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-31.translation: Having killed me, an innocent, with an arrow here, Kakutstha, what will you say among good people after this shameful deed?
ramayana-4-17-31.meaning: Vali asks how Rama will justify it.
ramayana-4-17-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)
