ramayana-4-17-32.translation: The killer of a king, of a brahmin, of cows, a thief, one who delights in killing living beings, an unbeliever, and one who marries before his elder brother all go to hell.
ramayana-4-17-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-33.translation: My skin cannot be worn by good people, my hair and bones are shunned, and my flesh is not to be eaten by the righteous like you.
ramayana-4-17-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-34.translation: Five five-clawed animals may be eaten by brahmins and kshatriyas, Raghava: the porcupine, the hedgehog, the monitor lizard, the hare and the tortoise.
ramayana-4-17-34.meaning: Vali cites the old food rules of the time.
ramayana-4-17-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-35.translation: The wise do not touch my skin or bones, king, and my flesh may not be eaten. Yet I, a five-clawed animal, have been killed.
ramayana-4-17-35.meaning: His death was without any lawful purpose.
ramayana-4-17-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-36.translation: With you as her protector, Kakutstha, the earth is unprotected, like a virtuous woman married to a scoundrel.
ramayana-4-17-36.meaning: Vali says the earth is ill served by Rama.
ramayana-4-17-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-37.translation: Deceitful, dishonest, petty, falsely humble, how were you, so wicked, born of the great Dasharatha?
ramayana-4-17-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-38.translation: I have been killed by the elephant Rama, who has broken the girth of good conduct, overstepped the dharma of the good, and thrown off the goad of righteousness.
ramayana-4-17-38.meaning: Vali calls Rama an elephant out of control.
ramayana-4-17-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-39.translation: If you had fought me in the open, prince, you would be seeing the god Yama today, killed by me.
ramayana-4-17-39.meaning: Vali says he would have won a fair fight.
ramayana-4-17-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-40.translation: But I, hard to overcome, was killed in battle by you unseen, like a drunk man asleep bitten by a snake.
ramayana-4-17-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-41.translation: If you killed me to please Sugriva, I could have tied Ravana by the neck and given him to you alive in battle.
ramayana-4-17-41.meaning: Vali would have been the stronger ally.
ramayana-4-17-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-42.translation: Whether Maithili were thrown into the sea or the underworld, at your command I would have brought her back like the white mare.
ramayana-4-17-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-43.translation: It is fitting that Sugriva should get the kingdom when I have gone to heaven. What is not fitting is that you killed me unrighteously in battle.
ramayana-4-17-43.meaning: Vali objects to the means, not the outcome.
ramayana-4-17-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-44.translation: The world is surely bound by Time in this way. If you have an answer that fits, think it over well.
ramayana-4-17-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-45.translation: Having said this, the great son of the king of gods, his mouth dry and in pain from the arrow, looked at Rama, bright as the sun, and fell silent.
ramayana-4-17-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-18-1.translation: Addressed by the stricken, fading Vali with words courteous yet harsh, full of dharma and meaning,
ramayana-4-18-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-2.translation: to him who was like the sun without light, a cloud emptied of rain, a quenched fire, having said his say,
ramayana-4-18-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-3.translation: to the matchless lord of monkeys, endowed with dharma and sense, Rama, having been reproached, spoke afterward.
ramayana-4-18-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-4.translation: Without understanding dharma, wealth, desire and the customs of the world, how can you in your childishness blame me here today?
ramayana-4-18-4.meaning: Rama says Vali judges without knowing.
ramayana-4-18-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-5.translation: Without asking wise elders respected by teachers, gentle one, you wish to speak to me out of a monkey's restlessness.
ramayana-4-18-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-6.translation: This land, with its mountains, woods and forests, belongs to the Ikshvakus, and so does the power to punish or favour its animals, birds and people.
ramayana-4-18-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-7.translation: Righteous Bharata rules it, truthful and straight, knowing the truth of dharma, desire and wealth, devoted to punishing and favouring rightly.
ramayana-4-18-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-8.translation: He in whom policy, discipline and truth are firmly set, and valour as seen, is a king who knows time and place.
ramayana-4-18-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-9.translation: Under his righteous command, we and other kings travel the whole earth, wishing to spread dharma.
ramayana-4-18-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-10.translation: While Bharata, tiger among kings and lover of dharma, rules the whole earth, who could act against dharma?
ramayana-4-18-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-11.translation: Standing firm in our own highest duty, honouring Bharata's command, we punish those who stray from the path, as the rules require.
ramayana-4-18-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-12.translation: But you have violated dharma, are condemned by your deeds, are ruled by desire, and have not kept to the path of a king.
ramayana-4-18-12.meaning: Rama says Vali broke the law.
ramayana-4-18-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-13.translation: An elder brother, a father, and one who gives knowledge: these three are to be regarded as fathers by those who walk the path of dharma.
ramayana-4-18-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-14.translation: A younger brother, one's own son, and a virtuous disciple: these three are to be regarded as sons, if dharma is the rule.
ramayana-4-18-14.meaning: Younger ones are owed a parent's care.
ramayana-4-18-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-15.translation: The dharma of the good is subtle and very hard to know, monkey. The Self in the hearts of all beings knows what is right and wrong.
ramayana-4-18-15.meaning: Dharma is subtle; conscience knows it.
ramayana-4-18-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-16.translation: Restless yourself, consulting with restless, undisciplined monkeys, what can you see, like one born blind consulting the born blind?
ramayana-4-18-16.meaning: Rama says Vali took poor counsel.
ramayana-4-18-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-17.translation: I will make the meaning of what I say clear to you. You should not blame me merely out of anger.
ramayana-4-18-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.
